producer_report.summary: Added a single path function, `paths::records_worktree(state_dir)`, which returns `<state>/records-worktree`. Added `RecordSet::load_dir` and `RecordSet::load_current` in athena-gate, and `Records::load_current` in store.rs. Each `load_current` reads the worktree when that directory exists, even if empty, and falls back to the treeish's `records/` only when it is absent. `Records::load_dir` now takes its `records/` half from `RecordSet::load_dir`. With a worktree, landings come only from `<worktree>/landings`; the doc comment says so. Moved exactly three call sites: the two loads in `Athena::status` (the per-class forecast `class_forecasts` reads the same loaded records) and the job lookup in `Athena::land_pr` (gh/landing.rs, which the request calls gh.rs). Added tests with distinct job ids and classes in the worktree and in-tree, each also run after removing the worktree. Added §14 to records-history.md, listing every remaining reader by file and function. Added a CHANGELOG entry. No scan test was added.

checks_run.note: 4 new tests: absent worktree equals load, existing worktree wins, empty existing worktree does not fall back, load_dir sorts and flags unknown files. First run failed on my wrong sort expectation; fixed and rerun with the full suite.
load_current reads the worktree when it exists and the tree when absent; an empty worktree does not fall back
status, forecast and land_pr tests, each with the worktree and again after removing it. The forecast test first failed because the fixture score used rules v1; it now uses athena_score::RULES.
Ran once. The tool printed no failure exit code. Its output was too large to read, so I did not read the per-test lines.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test, run with `cargo test`, puts job ids that differ between a records worktree and in-tree records/. It shows that Athena::status, the forecast and land_pr's job lookup each see the worktree's job ids and not the in-tree ones.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core records_worktree`: 3 passed. They are status::records_worktree_tests::status_records_worktree_decides_which_jobs_are_listed, ::forecast_records_worktree_decides_which_classes_are_headlined, and gh::tests::land_pr_records_worktree_decides_which_job_is_found. The in-tree job is TREE_JOB and the worktree job is WORKTREE_JOB. With the worktree present: status lists only WORKTREE_JOB; forecasts shows only class-wt; land_pr finds WORKTREE_JOB ('has no verification') and not TREE_JOB ('no job matches'). I did not run the tests against the old code.

criteria_check.criterion: A test run with `cargo test` removes the worktree directory and shows that status, the forecast and land_pr's lookup read the in-tree records/ job ids, as before the change.
criteria_check.evidence: The same three tests call remove_worktree (remove_dir_all of paths::records_worktree) and then assert that status lists only TREE_JOB, forecasts shows only class-tree, and land_pr finds TREE_JOB and no longer finds WORKTREE_JOB. They passed. The store.rs unit test also shows load_current with an absent path has the same job ids as Records::load.

criteria_check.evidence: `pub fn records_worktree(state_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf` sits right after repo_state_dir. Grep 'records-worktree' over crates/ matches only paths.rs: line 60, the construction, and line 133, its unit test.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/store.rs has Records::load_current and crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs has RecordSet::load_current. Each reads the worktree when it exists and falls back to the treeish's in-tree records/ only when the worktree is absent.
criteria_check.evidence: Both are `if worktree.is_dir() { load_dir(worktree) } else { load(git, treeish) }`. Unit tests in store.rs and the gate's records.rs cover the absent, existing and empty-existing cases; all passed.

A Grep for Records::load and RecordSet::load shows every other non-test caller unchanged. The request names landing.rs's land_pr as gh.rs.

criteria_check.evidence: New §14.2 has Groups A–E. I mapped each Grep hit of `Records::load(`, `RecordSet::load(`, `GitRecords::load(`, `JobFiles::load(` and `ls_tree_under(` (records, landings and records-subdirectory paths) to its enclosing function by reading the file's function list. The file readers come from Greps for read_dir and records-path joins. §14.2 names mistakes and trace in Group A; the request's 'mistake_report' is a free function that `mistakes` calls (the Records::load caller is `Athena::mistakes`), so Group A names `mistakes`, not mistake_report. No line numbers appear.

open_issues: The §14.2 list was built by reading Grep hits and function lists, with no scan test (out of scope). A reader that reaches records by another path (not Records::load/RecordSet::load/GitRecords::load/JobFiles::load, ls_tree_under or read_dir) could be missing.

Until a later slice creates the worktree, status and land_pr read `records/` as before. Once a worktree exists, drain.rs `records()` and other readers on HEAD can disagree with status and land_pr; §14 says so.
mistakes: First gate test expected the path order brief.md before brief-update-1.md; plain string order puts 'brief-' before 'brief.', so the assertion was wrong. Fixed.
First forecast fixture used score rules 'v1', which the commit gate refuses. Fixed by using athena_score::RULES.
I did not run the three new tests against the pre-change source to watch them fail.
learnings: `check_record_file` accepts `records/jobs/bootstrap/brief.md` and `brief-update-<n>.md` as valid Markdown, which makes small fixtures for loader tests.
The in-process commit gate refuses a Score whose `rules` is not a known version (it must be `athena_score::RULES`); a fixture with 'v1' is rejected.
A Job-only record (no Request) shows in status as 'interrupted', so it lands in both open and recent. Compare ids across both lists.

The `Athena` test fixture (`crate::code_health::tests::set_up()`) has a `StateDir` of a temp directory, so `paths::records_worktree(athena.state.root())` is controllable in tests with no global environment variable.
`land_pr` with no origin remote resolves the job and checks verification before touching the host, so an always-erroring Runner suffices for a lookup test.
desires: A shell tool that could read a saved tool-result file, or a pagination option on full `cargo test` output. Both the full-suite output and the long function lists were saved to files I could not open.
